review_scope: binary64 zero-tail invariant and restoring-state equivalence
accepted private residual and p64/p53 compatibility
generated initialization, restoring schedule, p64 tail, and XToF64 boundary
source, compiler, CPU-pack, and executable provenance

findings.issue: The direct model reused the accepted private residual and did not independently spill the mathematical p64 result.
Generated initialization and the complete p64/XToF64 tail were not checked despite exactness claims.
The calibration check excluded direct entries only while describing all control edges.
Two design-impossibility conclusions were emitted as constants rather than scoped implementation facts.

changes: Added an independent mathematical-p64-to-p53 spill comparison for every modeled positive finite binary64 input.
Added contiguous exact generated initialization and complete p64-tail assertions plus the post-root XToF64 call and normal spill sequence.
Narrowed calibration evidence to no direct entry/no fallthrough and rejected indirect call/jump instructions inside XRootCore.
Removed unsupported optimization-impossibility claims and retained only source-shaped facts about the measured candidate.

re_review.finding: The new p64 compatibility lemma assumed one mismatch direction, but binary64 input 0x3FF28C725373F0DC exhibits the reverse q versus q+1 direction while still spilling identically to p53.

changes: Made the p64 compatibility assertion direction-neutral: the two policy results differ by one and equal the set {q, q+1}.
Retained the explicit identical-p53 assertion for every p64-policy mismatch.
Regenerated model.json and production-layout.json with current verifier hashes while accepted Task #224 production was active.

final_review.method: read-only source/JSON/hash review plus independent reproduction of the reverse p64 case
